well: ODP Holes 195-1200A/B/D/E/F - SOUTH CHAMORRO SEAMOUNT, an active SERPENTINITE MUD VOLCANO on the Mariana forearc, North Pacific (13.783-13.784 N, 146.003 E; seafloor -2,910 to -2,931 m); ODP Leg 195 (2001), samples 0.15-108.71 mbsf; the seamount vents the most alkaline deep pore fluids known (pH ~12.5) and hosts a CORK observatory - the erupting mud IS mantle-wedge rock, ground and carried up 20+ km from the subducting Pacific plate interface
operator_on_log: Savov, Guggino, Ryan, Fryer & Mottl (USF/Hawaii) shore-based DCP emission spectrometry - major oxides, LOI and 11 trace elements on serpentine muds; drilling by JOIDES Resolution
source_database: PANGAEA, dataset doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.778374 ('(Table T2) Major and trace elements of serpentine muds from ODP Site 195-1200'); supplement to Savov et al. 2005, Proc. ODP Sci. Results 195, 1-49 (doi:10.2973/odp.proc.sr.195.103.2005)
license: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC-BY-3.0), declared IN the file's own header. Attribution: Savov/Guggino/Ryan/Fryer/Mottl / PANGAEA / ODP
fetch_method: read-only HTTPS fetch of the PANGAEA textfile export - COMPLETE dataset (432 data points per the header's own Size declaration, re-counted at gate time as non-empty body cells excluding Event + geocode columns, EXACT) in one fetch
coverage: COMPLETE DATASET: 22 samples across five holes - 20 with full major-oxide suites (SiO2/TiO2/Al2O3/Fe2O3T/MnO/MgO/CaO/Na2O/K2O + archived Total + LOI) and 2 trace-only rows; trace suite Sc/V/Cr/Ni/Sr/Ba/Zr/Y/B/Li; 19 samples carry the pure mantle-wedge serpentinite fingerprint (MgO 38.2-47.7%, Cr 1,942-3,748 ppm, Ni 2,648-6,162 ppm, LOI 13.0-21.2% structural water) and one is an exotic mafic clast riding in the mud
curves: Depth sed [m] 0.15-108.71 (GEOCODE; rows NOT in depth order - source ordering preserved)
SiO2..K2O major oxides [%] + archived Total [%] + LOI [%]
Sc V Cr Ni Sr Ba Zr Y B Li [mg/kg]
Event rides as per-row quality; sample labels verbatim
source_anomaly_disclosure: FOUR source quirks preserved verbatim: (1) the archived Total column closes against the sum of the nine listed oxides on 19 of 20 full rows (12 exact within 0.02, all within 0.07) but the EXOTIC CLAST row 1200D-8H-1,119-121 archives Total = 95.00 while its own listed oxides sum to 98.91 - a 3.91% internal discrepancy in the source (its published Total presumably includes components not carried into this table), pinned as the exception; (2) hole 195-1200B contributes core sample 2H-1,52-54 while the file's own event header declares '0 cores; 0 m cored; 0 m drilled' for that hole - an internal event-metadata contradiction; (3) several TiO2 cells archive below-detection as literal 0.00; (4) rows are not in depth order and two samples (9R-1,77-79 and 8H-1,127-129) carry only trace-element data with all oxides blank
purpose: thirty-seventh catalogue entry - the MARIANA FOREARC joins as region TWENTY-FIVE (the catalogue's first serpentinite mud volcano - a window through the forearc to the subducting plate 20+ km down, beside the South Chamorro CORK) and bulk-rock major/trace geochemistry is kind TWENTY-SIX; the mantle-wedge story is re-derived by the gate on every run: ALL 19 serpentinite rows pass the four-way fingerprint (ultramafic MgO, chromite Cr, mantle Ni, serpentine structural-water LOI) while the single exotic clast FAILS all four simultaneously (MgO 3.04, Cr 54, Ni 130, LOI 7.6 with TiO2 3.92 and Al2O3 21.16) - lithology classification by pure arithmetic - and the highest-Sr sample (1,756.6 ppm) is exactly the highest-CaO serpentinite (9.80%), the seafloor carbonate overprint appearing in two independent columns at once
verified: 22 rows / 432 counted cells against the header's own Size declaration (EXACT); oxide-sum closure re-derived on all 20 full rows (19 within 0.07, the exotic clast's 3.91 internal discrepancy disclosed and pinned); serpentinite fingerprint 19/19 vs exotic 0/4; Sr-max = CaO-max coincidence pinned to sample 1200D-1H-1,15-17; the 1200B zero-cores contradiction pinned; gate-pinned; source URL serves the identical dataset
